cards.text: Job and his friends have been going back and forth for a while. Now Job picks it right back up and keeps going. Baker, this man is NOT done talking.
He opens with an oath, "As surely as God lives," and in the same breath he says the Almighty has deprived him of justice and embittered his soul.

cards.question: Job makes a promise that lasts as long as there's breath in him. What does he promise his lips won't do?
Job tells his friends he's finally ready to admit they've been right.

cards.text: No way. Job says he'll maintain his integrity until he dies, and he'll cling to his righteousness and never let go, like a baker holding the last cookie in the box while the whole family reaches for it.

cards.question: As long as Job lives, he says one thing won't accuse him. What is it?

cards.text: Then Job says, "May my enemy be like the wicked and my opponent like the unjust." And he asks what hope the godless man has when God takes away his life.

cards.question: Job keeps asking about the godless man. When distress comes on him, what does Job wonder?
Job also asks whether the godless man will delight in the Almighty and call on God at all times.

cards.text: Now Job switches into teacher mode. He says, "I will instruct you in the power of God."

cards.question: Job tells his friends they've all seen God's ways for themselves. So why do they keep up all this ___ talk?

cards.text: Empty talk. Like a group chat with ninety new messages and not ONE of them answers the question.
Now Job lays out the wicked man's portion from God, what the ruthless receive from the Almighty. And baker, this is not a thank-you card.

cards.question: Job says the wicked man's many sons will live long and peaceful lives.
Job keeps going: the wicked man's survivors end up buried by the plague. How do their widows respond?

cards.text: Next, his stuff. He heaps up silver like dust and piles up clothes like clay, and I lived under dust for YEARS, baker, so trust me, that is a LOT of silver.

cards.question: Job says the righteous end up wearing what the wicked man laid up.

cards.text: And the house he built? Job says it's like a moth's cocoon, like a hut set up by a watchman.

cards.question: Job compares the wicked man's house to a moth's cocoon and a watchman's hut. What's the point of those pictures?
The wicked man lies down ___ but when he opens his eyes all is gone.

cards.text: Go to bed with a full cookie box, wake up to crumbs. Then terrors overtake him like a flood, and the east wind carries him away.

cards.question: Job says the wind shows the wicked man mercy as he runs from it.
As the wicked man is driven out, Job says the wind does one more thing to him. What is it?

cards.text: Claps and hisses him out of his place. That's not applause, baker, that's a whole room booing you out the door. And Job? Friend, he's still not done talking.

findings.problem: The right answer, Speak wickedness, comes only from Job 27:4. The card cites Job 27:3-4, which is wider than the right answer's verse. Verse 3 is only the setup in the question.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats the empty talk from Job 27:12, which card 11 already asked and answered, and adds a joke. It doesn't tell any new part of the passage or move the baker forward. It is a recap card carrying a joke.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The question asks what the moth's cocoon and the watchman's hut pictures mean. Both pictures come only from Job 27:18. The card cites Job 27:18-19, which is wider than the right answer's verse. Verse 19 is about the man waking up with nothing, not the pictures, and card 8 cites it for its own question.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: Card 10 has already shown that the wind shows the wicked man no mercy. That rules out both wrong answers, Lifts him to safety and Sets him down gently, so the baker can pick the right answer by elimination. The wrong answers should be things a merciless wind could plausibly do, so they aren't ruled out by the setup.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
